episode_profile.title: Gordon Crovitz: Will AI SPREAD Misinformation & Fake News?
episode_profile.topic_summary: In this episode, Craig Smith interviews Gordon Crovitz about the challenges of misinformation in the age of AI. They discuss how NewsGuard's databases help identify unreliable news sources and the implications of AI-generated content on the spread of misinformation.

key_arguments.claim: AI-generated content is the fastest growing segment of information on the internet, which poses a significant risk to the accuracy of AI models.
key_arguments.speaker: Gordon Crovitz
key_arguments.context: Crovitz highlights the increasing prevalence of AI-generated misinformation and its potential impact on public discourse.

key_arguments.claim: NewsGuard has identified 557 unreliable AI-enhanced news sites that generate misinformation.
key_arguments.speaker: Gordon Crovitz
key_arguments.context: Crovitz explains how these sites are created for financial gain through programmatic advertising.

key_arguments.claim: Generative AI models can enhance the work of malign actors by creating believable misinformation.
key_arguments.speaker: Gordon Crovitz
key_arguments.context: Crovitz discusses a specific example of AI-generated misinformation that was mistaken for a legitimate news story.

key_arguments.claim: The spread of misinformation generated by AI is likely to grow at a geometric rate as it becomes part of the training data for future AI models.
key_arguments.speaker: Gordon Crovitz
key_arguments.context: Crovitz expresses concern about the compounding effect of AI-generated misinformation on future AI training.

key_arguments.claim: Microsoft's Bing Chat has successfully integrated NewsGuard's data to improve its ability to identify and mitigate misinformation.
key_arguments.speaker: Gordon Crovitz
key_arguments.context: Crovitz contrasts Bing's approach with other AI models that have not utilized trust data effectively.

key_arguments.claim: There is a significant financial incentive for creating AI-generated misinformation sites, which complicates efforts to combat them.
key_arguments.speaker: Gordon Crovitz
key_arguments.context: Crovitz discusses the economic motivations behind the proliferation of unreliable AI-generated news.

content_chapters.title: Introduction to NewsGuard
content_chapters.summary: Gordon Crovitz introduces NewsGuard and its mission to combat misinformation.

content_chapters.title: Identifying AI-Generated Content
content_chapters.summary: Crovitz discusses the challenges and methods used to identify AI-generated news sites.

content_chapters.title: Impact of Misinformation on AI Models
content_chapters.summary: The conversation explores how misinformation affects the training and reliability of AI models.

content_chapters.title: Bing Chat vs. Other AI Models
content_chapters.summary: Crovitz compares Bing Chat's use of NewsGuard data to other AI models' handling of misinformation.

content_chapters.title: Future of Misinformation and AI
content_chapters.summary: Crovitz shares his thoughts on the future challenges posed by AI-generated misinformation.

citations.reference: European Commission's Code of Practice on Disinformation
citations.context: Crovitz mentions NewsGuard's involvement in this voluntary code to address misinformation.

notable_moments: Crovitz's example of AI-generated misinformation about Netanyahu's psychiatrist highlights the dangers of generative AI.
Crovitz expresses skepticism about social media platforms' willingness to address misinformation.
